overall: The AG found violations for two notices lacking names (July 19/26 and Sept 20), insufficient October 18 minutes, and failure to review an October complaint before counsel responded; other allegations were dismissed or declined as untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Committee did not allow members of the public to speak during meetings.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation, but rather gives the chair of the public body discretion to decide whether to permit public comment during a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Committee discussed executive session matters in open session.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that, even if taken as true, the allegation that the Committee discussed an executive session matter in open session while the purpose for the executive session may still have been ongoing does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged that meeting topics requested by Committee members were left off the notices.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require the chair to add topics to a meeting notice that are requested by fellow members of the public body.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged executive session notices for May 17, June 8, June 21, June 24 and June 28, 2023 lacked specificity by omitting names; complaints were filed late.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaints were filed more than 30 days after each alleged violation was reasonably discoverable, we find the allegations with respect to these five meetings to be untimely and decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged notices for August 11, September 1, 6, 18 and 29, 2023 lacked specificity; no executive session was held on those dates.
allegations.key_passage: we find no violation with respect to the sufficiency of the executive session topics listed on the notices.

allegations.summary: July 19 and July 26, 2023 notices identified the 'Interim Chief of Schools Officer' by title only, without the name of the person under consideration.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify on both the July 19, 2023, and July 26, 2023, meeting notices the name of the specific nonunion personnel

allegations.summary: September 20 and November 15, 2023 notices cited Purpose 3 (litigation) for discussing an Open Meeting Law complaint.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the notices included sufficient information from which the public could conclude that the topics was appropriate for executive session, and therefore sufficiently advised the public of the anticipated discussions.

allegations.summary: The September 20, 2023 notice did not identify the name of the person who filed the Open Meeting Law complaint, unlike the November 15 notice.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify the name of the person who filed the Open Meeting Law complaint on the notice of the meeting held on September 20, 2023.

allegations.summary: October 18, 2023 minutes said a named person 'registered and spoke' but gave no summary of the public comments made during the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board created insufficient minutes and violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to include any summary of the statements.

allegations.summary: An October 4, 2023 Open Meeting Law complaint was answered by counsel without the Committee first reviewing it at a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We are constrained to find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when it did not first meet to review the complaint before legal counsel responded.

remedy: Revise and approve the minutes of the October 18, 2023 meeting within thirty days of the letter, per the guidance given.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements; similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee to revise and approve the minutes of the October 18, 2023, meeting within thirty days of the date of this letter in accordance with the guidance provided above.
